correctness.rationale: Exact color-partition enumeration gives E_n(q). Bridge factorization is valid for arbitrary signs and attached tree shapes. Formal coefficient extraction gives h_3=2-(n+1)E_n(1) for r=0 and h_4=2^r E_n(3)-2(n+r+1) for r≥1. The binomial expansion of (2e^z-1)^{q/2} gives E_n(1)>0 for odd n and the exact rational 731229629/679477248>1 proves E_n(3)<0 for every odd n≥7. Direct polynomial evaluations yield the nonnegative one-bridge H for n=3,5; the Eulerian differential recurrence preserves nonnegativity for all further bridges. All ranges, cases and strict inequalities are addressed; verify.py independently checks exact computations and finite boundary cases.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the sharp odd-order classification of chromatic-numerator nonnegativity after arbitrary bridge-only attachments, not the classical zero-free chromatic polynomial of a signed clique. A formal odd-palette sign evaluation, a uniform eight-term rational certificate and a positivity-preserving Eulerian operator establish an infinite boundary not stated in inspected sources. Prior signed-clique enumeration is credited. Searches produced no exact or stronger covering assertion; unindexed prior work is a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 balancing-vertex criterion and its signed K4 balanced-bridge counterexample motivate whether arbitrary balanced-tree attachments can restore chromatic-numerator positivity. The theorem gives a complete sharp answer for every odd all-negative clique, exposing a persistent order-seven barrier despite arbitrarily many balanced blocks. The key formal-palette sign mechanism and the bridge-preserving positivity operator explain the phase structurally; an infinite classification is not a routine fixed-n table. It does not claim an all-graph equivalence or a paper-sized general classification.
